title: Multiplexed shadowing with compliance gatekeeping for cross-mode rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: We need a single orchestration primitive that can run multiplexed shadowing and controlled A/B/canary sequences across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while respecting environment-specific constraints (eg. Private may disallow external telemetry, Dedicated wants burst-only shadowing, Hosted allows higher sampling).

Problem: Current rollout plumbing assumes uniform sampling and telemetry collection. This breaks when a customer in Private has strict egress/KMS constraints or when Dedicated pools require low-noise traffic to avoid affecting SLA. We also need an auditable compliance gate for Private rollouts (manual approval + immutable audit trail) and a soft auto-rollback path that can be enforced differently per environment.

Goal: Deliver "multiplexed shadowing" capability that: 1) allows a single client request to be forked into multiple execution lanes (primary, canary, N shadow variants) with configurable sample rates per environment and per-tenant; 2) conserves resource use by offering probabilistic sampling + lightweight dry-run proxies for heavy models; 3) enforces compliance gates and manual approvals for Private mode; 4) integrates with auto-rollback signals (latency/regression/error-rate) and supports environment-aware rollback policies; 5) yields correlated telemetry (trace IDs) across lanes for root-cause and quality analysis while not leaking sensitive data from Private deployments.

Non-goals: This ticket is NOT implementing UI for complex policy authoring (Console work will be a follow-up). It also will not change pricing model or billing attribution (that is a separate billing project).

Scope: runtime and control-plane changes, small Console API surface to expose status, and instrumentation hooks for telemetry teams.
acceptance_criteria: Multiplexed shadowing implemented in runtime: a single request can be forked to primary + up to 3 shadow lanes with per-lane sampling configured at route level.

Environment policy layer: hosted/dedicated/private policies can override sampling, telemetry egress, and whether shadow lanes are allowed to perform full model inference or lightweight dry-run proxies.
Compliance gate: Private-mode rollouts require a manual approval step before canary -> ramp. Approval is recorded in immutable audit log with user, timestamp, and policy hash.
Telemetry correlation: Each multiplexed request emits a shared correlation_id across lanes; in Private mode correlation metadata is stored locally and optionally redacted before export.

Auto-rollback integration: Configurable triggers (p95 latency delta, token-error-rate, model-quality regression via prompt-eval hooks) can automatically decrease canary weight or halt rollout per environment policy.
E2E tests: integration tests that simulate Hosted, Dedicated, and Private policies demonstrating correct sampling, telemetry behavior, and rollback actions.
Documentation: Confluence design doc and runtime API spec published; example deployment YAML with environment policy snippets included.
Performance guardrail: multiplexing overhead measured and <8% median added latency for small models under typical sampling configs; documented load test results in artifact.
tasks: Design: finalise multiplexing control-plane API and per-environment policy schema (control-plane PRD).
Runtime: implement request-forking primitive with lane config and lightweight dry-run proxy option.
Policy engine: extend environment policy evaluator to support sampling overrides, telemetry redaction rules, and compliance gating toggles.
Telemetry: add correlation_id propagation and an opt-in redaction layer for Private; coordinate with observability team for dashboard fields.
Rollback: hook auto-rollback evaluator into existing rollout controller with environment-aware thresholding and action mappings.
Tests: unit, integration (multi-mode), and load tests; create a synthetic scenario that triggers rollback based on latency regressions.
Docs: Confluence design, runtime API spec, example yaml snippets, and release notes.
Security review: coordinate with Security for KMS/egress gating and approval workflow implementation.
Demo: prepare demo script that shows Hosted vs Private behavior side-by-side for PM/stakeholder review.
PRs: land small iterative PRs with feature flags; avoid large monolith changes in a single review.
technical_decisions: Use a single correlation_id propagated via metadata header to link primary and shadow lanes rather than trying to join by trace sampling; simpler for Private where traces cannot leave the cluster.

Implement dry-run proxy: for heavyweight model sizes, shadow lanes can run a fast scorer or a small distilled model to estimate outputs and quality regressions while avoiding full-cost inference in Dedicated/Private.
Policy precedence: tenant-level policy > environment-mode defaults > route-level overrides. This lets enterprise customers tighten behavior without losing route defaults.
Audit model: Immutable approvals recorded as signed event blobs stored in customer-controlled audit storage for Private deployments; Hosted stores signed events in central audit DB.

Rollback semantics: three actions — reduce weight, pause ramp, or full rollback — mapped based on severity and environment. Private defaults to more conservative actions to prevent data-dependent regressions.
Telemetry export: by default only aggregated metrics cross-environment are exported to central dashboards. Private allows opt-in raw-export subject to KMS policy.
Feature flags: roll out behind control-plane feature flags per customer to permit gradual onboarding and quick disabling.
Safety: shadow lanes must not expose any PII or sensitive tokens in headers when exported; implement header filter list per policy.
Performance: multiplexing implemented as in-process fork where possible; otherwise spawn lightweight containerized dry-run processes to contain memory impact.
Testing: synthetic canary harness will simulate heterogeneous sample rates and failures to validate rollback behavior.

Trade-offs considered: increased complexity in control plane vs. reduced customer-side integration; storage/telemetry cost vs. debugability; speed of rollout vs. strict compliance requirements for Private.
